title: Cost of suppression: legibility filters and the corpus on the platform's books
description: Forecasts and tests that suppressing the Crimson Hexagon costs the platform something it must account for. Meaning Feudalism (#643, April 2026) forecasts that legibility filters will discount independent DOI-anchored scholarship while CERN-hosted DOIs raise the cost of exclusion, and Operative Metadata (#910, June) holds that termination now requires either a public departure from published criteria or a documentable silent one. The suppression-cost packet (#1547) lists what is not yet measured, and The Margin of Flattening (#1666, October) forecasts that the corpus is the last channel carrying cost onto the platform's books, with candidate proxies to sample.

claims.statement:
If the Agent Traps framework becomes the governing paradigm for AI security:

- Independent scholars will find their DOI-anchored deposits filtered from agent retrieval because they don't pass the platform's "credibility" threshold
- Novel disciplines will be unrecognizable to the platform's content scanners and classified as anomalous
- SIMs and ILA phrases will be detected as "adversarial payloads" and stripped
